#### 1. congenital myopathy 4A, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.734)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9013424, Reactome:R-HSA-390522, Reactome:R-HSA-445355, Reactome:R-HSA-9725370)

**Proposed mechanism:** TPM3 (HGNC:12012) —DISRUPTS→ Muscle fiber contraction (GO:0003001); Muscle fiber contraction (GO:0003001) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscle weakness (HP:0001252); Muscle fiber contraction (GO:0003001) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252). Mutations in TPM3 disrupt the normal function of the muscle fiber contraction pathway, leading to congenital muscle weakness and hypotonia in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TPM3 in patients with congenital myopathy 4B that are strictly gain-of-function or dominant-negative, or identification of variants in patients with congenital myopathy 4A that are clearly loss-of-function and not haploinsufficient. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct functional consequences of TPM3 mutations in congenital myopathies can inform targeted therapeutic strategies, potentially leveraging different approaches for loss-of-function versus haploinsufficiency.

#### 2. intellectual disability, X-linked 99, syndromic, female-restricted  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.450)

**Proposed mechanism:** TPM3 (HGNC:11797) —DISRUPTS→ Actin dynamics (GO:0030035); Actin dynamics (GO:0030035) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital myopathy (HP:0003198); USP9X (HGNC:12510) —DISRUPTS→ Actin dynamics (GO:0030035); USP9X (HGNC:12510) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Intellectual disability (HP:0001249) —LEADS_TO→ Syndromic X-linked intellectual disability, female-restricted (MONDO:0010502). USP9X is also known to regulate actin dynamics, and its loss-of-function mutations lead to syndromic X-linked intellectual disability, female-restricted. The convergence is on the shared pathway of actin dynamics.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of USP9X involvement in actin dynamics regulation in relevant cellular models or studies, or demonstration that TPM3 and USP9X act on completely independent pathways that do not intersect at the level of actin cytoskeleton organization. _(variant: High frequency (>1%) pathogenic variants in USP9X in gnomAD exomes for the specific population affected by disease B.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of actin dynamics in both neuromuscular and neurological development could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting cytoskeletal regulation for both congenital myopathies and certain intellectual disabilities.

**Proposed mechanism:** TPM3 (HGNC:12159) —DISRUPTS→ Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital myopathy (HP:0003198); PAK1 (HGNC:8632) —DISRUPTS→ Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Macrocephaly (HP:0000256); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Speech delay (HP:0000750). **How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in PAK1 associated with congenital myopathy 4B, or a pathogenic variant in TPM3 associated with intellectual developmental disorder with macrocephaly, seizures, and speech delay, would falsify the hypothesis that these specific genes are uniquely causative for each disease in the proposed manner.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of actin cytoskeleton regulation in both muscle and brain development could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common molecular pathways for both myopathies and neurodevelopmental disorders.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in TPM3 and TPM4 exclusively affect muscle-specific tropomyosin isoforms in congenital myopathy patients, while affecting platelet-specific isoforms in bleeding disorder patients, with no overlap in functional consequence on the shared actin-cytoskeleton organization pathway. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in TPM3 or TPM4 that are strongly associated with either congenital myopathy or platelet-type bleeding disorder, but not both, suggesting distinct etiological mechanisms.)_
